title: A Toolchain File That Cannot Lie: Generating It From the Triple, Checking It, and the Setting That Links the Host's Libraries Into the Robot

questions.question: Why generate the toolchain file from the triple?
options: One source of truth: the system name, processor and compilers follow from the triple, and a hand edit cannot make them disagree
questions.explanation: The same spec gave the same text every time.

questions.question: What does -march=native mean in a cross build?
options: The CPU of the machine doing the compiling, so the binary may use instructions the robot does not have, with no error

questions.question: The sysroot has no libusb and the host has one for x86_64. What do ONLY and BOTH do?
options: ONLY says it is missing, which is right; BOTH returns the host's x86_64 library without a word

questions.question: Why are programs found on the host and libraries in the sysroot only?
options: A program that runs during the build must run on the machine building, while a library is linked into the robot's binary and must be built for the robot

questions.question: Why does validate refuse a backslash in a Windows sysroot?
options: CMake reads a backslash as an escape, so the path is not the one written

questions.question: What is the one real check of a toolchain file that this lesson cannot make?
options: Running the cross compiler and looking at what the binary was built for with file or readelf: the repository's CI has no cross compiler
questions.explanation: The text and the checks are tested, not CMake's acceptance.
